newsitem.title: south korea: NKorea defector warns of nuclear attack threat-paper.
newsitem.headline: NKorea defector warns of nuclear attack threat-paper.

text.p: North Korea has the ability to turn South Korea into a "sea of flames" with a nuclear attack, a South Korean newspaper on Tuesday quoted Pyongyang defector Hwang Jang-yop as saying in a report.

The report carried in the Chosun Ilbo also quoted Hwang, who arrived in Seoul on Sunday, as saying North Korea believed it could win a war against the South and planned to annihilate Japan if the United States tried to intervene.
The newspaper, which often publishes scoops based on intelligence sources, said Hwang wrote the report last August before he became the most senior official ever to flee his impoverished country.
He defected in Beijing on February 12.
"The North can turn the South into a sea of flames and annihilate it by using nuclear and chemical weapons and rockets," the report said.
"The North believes if it wages war it will no doubt win, and if the United States intervenes, it plans to scorch Japan, although reaching mainland America would be questionable."
Political analysts said it was not certain from the phrasing of the document whether Hwang was stating that the North possesed nuclear bombs.

Fears that North Korea was producing an atomic bomb sparked a crisis which was defused when Pyongyang agreed in 1994 to dismantle its nuclear facilities in return for safer reactors promised by the United States.

According to some U.S. intelligence reports, North Korea may have acquired enough weapons grade plutonium from a graphite reactor in Yongbyon, near Pyongyang, to build one or two nuclear bombs before engineers began mothballing the facility. No hard evidence has been offered.
One Seoul-based Western diplomat said Hwang's reported comments on nuclear war should be treated with caution.
"I wouldn't take it as gospel," he said. "I'm not certain Hwang would have been in the right position to have that kind of information."
The comments, he added "are a bit overblown".
For decades, Hwang was North Korea's chief ideologue who crafted a philosophy of self-reliance which he says has mutated into a mix of feudalism and militarism.
During the nuclear crisis preceding the landmark 1994 nuclear agreement between Washington and Pyongyang, the North often threatened to turn the South into a "sea of flames".
U.S. and South Korean officials assume North Korea has chemical and possibly biological weapons. It has Scud missiles targeted at the South.
Earlier this month, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda quoted unconfirmed reports as saying North Korea may have deployed ballistic missiles capable of hitting most of Japan.
Hwang arrived in Seoul as a self-proclaimed saviour of the Korean people. He said on Sunday his mission was to avert a war that North Korea was bent on unleashing against the South.
The two Koreas are still technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended with a truce rather than a peace treaty.
"The leadership in the North is now standing at a cross-roads between staging the great tragedy in the history of our people by mobilising military force and surrendering," the August report said.
Hwang described North Korean leader Kim Jong-il as clever but capricious, a jealous man and a dictator.
"It is clear without any doubt that an historic tragedy is approaching our people," the report said.
It warned that the North maintained a huge network of moles in the South and that the West must not expect its repressive communist system to implode naturally.
